summary: Frozen-source review found four ownership/lifecycle defects. No writes or runtime checks performed. Candidate fixes require parent validation.

findings.claim: stop closes the listener between acceptLoop's epoch check and accept; fd reuse can make the old loop consume another listener's connection or block its serial queue.
findings.recommendation: Use nonblocking acceptance and a sole listener-close owner. Force the check/accept interleaving and fd reuse; verify new and unrelated listeners remain usable.

findings.claim: Death after bind but before durable identity recording leaves an unknown public endpoint that prevents subsequent cooperative startup. Truncating the lease record creates another crash window.
findings.recommendation: Validate private staged publication and durable alternating records. Kill at each publication/persistence boundary and verify restart, including repeated crashes. Confirm Darwin pathname publication semantics.

findings.claim: Suspended old handlers retain connections entries across stop/restart. At maximumConnections they indefinitely prevent new admission; the I/O deadline does not bound handleIPC.
findings.recommendation: Define worker cancellation/draining and count capacity by epoch while preserving single-worker close ownership. Latch one handler with capacity one, restart the same server, and test new admission before releasing the old handler.

findings.claim: The lease initializer assigns its stored fd, explicitly closes on validation/flock failure, then deinit closes again. Concurrent fd reuse can close another owner's descriptor.
findings.recommendation: Keep the fd local until validation and flock succeed, with exactly one failure cleanup. Test insecure and contended lock failures with close tracking or forced reuse.
